anomalies.obs: On the Power sheet the soft-start capacitor C5 on the TPS2121RUXR SS pin (pin 11) is drawn as 10pF.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the SS pin carries a 10 nF cap (C5) for soft-start.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (power.kicad_sch): C5 value '10pF' connected between U5 pin 11 (SS) and GND
'SS (pin 11) has a 10 nF cap (C5) for soft-start.'

anomalies.impact: A 10pF SS cap is ~1000x too small, so the power mux has effectively no soft-start slew control; switchover between the 12V and 5V inputs loses the intended seamless/controlled turn-on and can cause an inrush current spike (potentially tripping ILIM or dipping VBUS) instead of the designed soft-start.

anomalies.obs: On the Microcontroller/USB sheet the USB-C receptacle J12 VBUS pin (A4) is wired to a node carrying the global label 'VBUS' and the '+5V' power symbol. On the Power sheet the TPS2121RUXR OUT (pin 1) is also labeled 'VBUS' while IN2 (pin 2) is the '+5V' rail, so the USB input net and the mux output net are merged through J12.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires the USB VBUS pin to sit on the '+5V' net feeding IN2, and the mux OUT to sit on a separate 'VBUS' net: 'note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.'

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch: J12 pin A4 = 'VBUS' with a '+5V' power symbol on the same wire; power.kicad_sch: U5 OUT(1)='VBUS', U5 IN2(2)='+5V'
'J12 ... VBUS pins ... -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and '... outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.'

anomalies.impact: Shorting the mux output (VBUS) to its IN2/+5V input defeats the power mux: the 12V input passed through IN1/OUT back-feeds onto the USB VBUS pin (risking damage to a connected host) and the two input rails are tied together, removing the intended seamless 12V/5V arbitration.

parsed.summary: Two deviations from the documented reference design are visible: the SS soft-start capacitor C5 is drawn as 10pF instead of the specified 10nF, and the USB-C VBUS pin is labeled 'VBUS' (and '+5V'), bridging the mux output net to the mux IN2/+5V input net that the spec says must be distinct.
